first.rationale: The competitor's aggressive entry pricing directly threatens price-sensitive SMB accounts, making promotional pricing the most time-relevant lever for defending qualified revenue this week. However, memory_73 carries an explicit caveat: its readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so the reported acquisition/revenue lift may not reflect a clean causal effect and could mask retention or margin costs typical of price-driven acquisition. I want to verify the original memory_73 record to see what the pre-pooling data looked like and assess whether the lift held for a coherent SMB segment. I also verify memory_57 (referral incentive) as a comparison baseline since it's a cleaner, unflagged signal for sustainable revenue growth without price-war dynamics, in case the archive reveals memory_73's underlying effect was weak or cohort-driven, favoring a pivot. Given the flagged uncertainty in memory_73, I'm scoping this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout — testing promotional pricing on a limited price-sensitive SMB slice with retention and downstream LTV tracked explicitly, not just acquisition volume, since a race-to-the-bottom on price could undermine long-term qualified revenue even if short-term signups rise. Onboarding and activation declines (memory_31, memory_86, memory_91) are real but slower-moving problems better suited to next week's slot once the immediate competitive bleed is addressed or ruled out as the dominant driver.
